scope: Q7 v1.01 original-token reserialization, one bounded rebuilt code experiment, application update-file gate and E01 burn-header dispatch. All results are offline.

verification: all decoded bytes match requested regions
original file and ELF segment positions/sizes preserved
limitations: No package relocation, code insertion/deletion or general compressor is implemented.
Missing literal codes or payload capacity are rejected, never silently truncated.
The expanded ELF is for analysis only; not a camera image.
Footer checksum and software decoding do not prove updater, boot or camera acceptance.

roundtrip.method: Re-emit consumed original token bits and validated zero padding. Preserve every compiled table and fixed block slot. All four decoded payloads and complete package/ELF bytes match.

patch_experiment.package_diff_bound: All changed package bytes are within E04 block 146 or the four-byte footer checksum field.
patch_experiment.method: Replace invalid original literals/copies with available original-table literals and retain valid tokens including cross-block history. Both bitstreams fit the same original payload slot. Independently re-decode all four segments and compare the complete rebuilt analysis ELF.

app_gate.checksum_rule: Sum of unsigned body bytes before the last 32 bytes, modulo 2^32. Read stored sum as little-endian u32.
app_gate.result: 1 when the exercised file operations and three string comparisons succeed and body sum matches. Version bytes are excluded from the body checksum and not checked by this gate.
app_gate.exercised: 13 modeled file/allocator cases. Getter, string compare and byte-sum instructions execute from the pinned original ELF. Real original and rebuilt package sums were separately compared to their footers.

limits: Synthetic 96-byte files exercise the original gate and checksum loop; no checksum-loop stub.
Real package byte sums are checked separately in repack_q7.
Application file gate only: no flash service, bootloader, hardware decoder, boot or shooting.

boot_image.mapping: VA is scoped to E01 here. File offsets are absolute offsets in the original update and use E01 PT_LOAD file-backed ranges.

boot_dispatch.hash_field: u16 header+0x3c truncated to handle byte +0x1278
boot_dispatch.exercised: Five original BurnGetHandle replays, with allocator and diagnostics modeled. A nonnull handle establishes dispatch selection only.
boot_dispatch.optional_md5: After earlier Burn media and callback checks, nonzero handle+0x1278 takes the queue/worker setup path. BurnHashManager uses MD5 init/append/finish and a 16-byte compare. The original supplied header selects zero for this optional path. No execution of Burn or the MD5 worker was part of these replays.

limits: Rebuilt function is a controlled metadata-return experiment, not an AF/UI feature patch.
BurnGetHandle replay stops before any flash callback, queue or hardware operation.
The supplied header selects BurnNand with its optional MD5-worker flag zero; this does not rule out later checks.
No camera updater, boot, capture or recovery was exercised.

reproduction.instructions: Save patch_input as the JSON array at patch_input_path. Install angr in the Python environment for the two replay commands. Output paths must be new.

evidence.role: Application caller checks the gate before LoadFirmware/UpdateFirmware dispatch
Application file gate size, open, footer seek and 32-byte read
GetCodeName, GetKBNumber and GetProductNumber and comparisons at footer+0/+8/+16
Little-endian footer sum and native unsigned byte-sum loop, exact equality and success return
Original GetFirmwareReleaseVersion return and delay-slot instruction
Card path creates the burn handle and invokes Burn as separate steps
BurnGetHandle reads header kind and copies header+0x3c low byte to handle+0x1278
Original boot jump-table slots for kinds 3, 5, 7 and 8
Boot switch arms load and write the BurnNand, BurnSdMmc and BurnLbaNand callbacks
Burn selects optional nonzero-flag queue/worker setup, then executes the selected callback
Optional MD5 worker append, init, finish and 16-byte compare calls

file_evidence.role: Burn header optional hash halfword at +0x3c and adjacent halfword at +0x3e
App footer four version bytes at +0x1c

trace_limitations: Extents end at the next distinct sidecar address, not a typed ELF function size.
Linear MIPS32 word scan; edges are instruction candidates, not proof of reachability.
Delay slots are included in extents. Register-indirect targets are unresolved.
A jump is recorded as a transfer, not automatically a function call.
E01 function bounds come from original typed ELF32 symbols rather than main sidecar windows.
E01 and main can share VAs. Verify E01 witnesses against the E01 PT_LOAD map or the recorded original offset.
File-only header/footer witnesses use original file offsets without a runtime VA.
limitations: The reserializer supports guarded same-size edits only. Missing original-table literals or insufficient capacity stop the rebuild. It does not relocate, append/delete code, or regenerate tables.
The changed function is a controlled release-metadata return experiment. It neither changes footer version bytes nor establishes a working AF or UI patch.
File-gate success, BurnGetHandle selection and the zero optional MD5-worker flag apply only to the observed branches. Other updater, section, boot or hardware checks remain possible.
No updater, flash write, camera boot, recovery or hardware decode was exercised in these checks.

validation.verification: Compared each word against original E01/E03 bytes or hash-verified decoded segment bytes; independently checked absolute or decoded offsets.
